Hi Maya — thanks for the quick report and the logs. We’ve triaged this and are treating it as a high-priority performance incident. Monica (CS) and Laura (Platform Ops) are looped in.

Immediate items:
- Short-term mitigation you can try now: switch the chat route to poll mode (stream: false) for the affected clients — this will smooth perceived latency while we stabilize streaming.
- Alternative quick fix: reduce `max_tokens` from 1024 -> 512 and set `response_chunk_bytes: 512` to force smaller, more frequent chunks.
- We have requested the Redwood telemetry team to pull the server-side traces for the US-WEST edge cluster (edges/us-west-2).

We’ll follow up within the hour with telemetry and a recommended action plan. I’m sorry for the disruption — we’ll make this right.

Hi Maya — quick technical guidance from ops while we pull traces: 

Observations from the logs you sent:
- Websocket reconnections in the 08:42–08:46 window correlated with elevated queue depth on the streaming workers in us-west-2.
- A subset of streaming sessions showed a backlog in the KV cache population step that can cause token batching at emission time.

Temporary mitigations (copy/paste):
1) cURL fallback (switch to polling):
   curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/responses \n     -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' \n     -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n     -d '{"model":"redwood-7b-prod","input":"<prompt>","stream":false,"max_tokens":512}'

2) If you must keep streaming: set `max_tokens:512` and `response_chunk_bytes:512` in the SDK to force smaller writes; set `prefer_edge: \"us-east-1\"` to route to a less impacted edge while we stabilize.

3) Retry/backoff: implement an exponential backoff on websocket reconnects with a jitter (start 250ms, max 3s) — this reduces thundering reconnects to the same edge shard.

We’ve attached a short telemetry snippet from our side (realtime-telemetry-snippet.json) and created SR-77123 in our tracker. I’ll keep you posted as we get the full postmortem.

— Monica
Customer Success, Redwood Inference

From: priyom_das@redwood.com

Subject: Follow-up & next steps — SR-77123 (chatflow throttling incident)

Hi Maya — quick follow-up now that we have the short-term telemetry and a preliminary RCA. Summary:
- Incident window: 2027-11-03 08:42–09:05 PST.
- Impact: elevated token emission latency for ~18% of streaming sessions in edges/us-west-2; symptoms were bursty token delivery and websocket reconnects.
- Root cause (prelim): a combination of a rollout of a prioritized batching change to a subset of streaming shards + concurrent client reconnect storms that caused worker queue saturation. The batching change intended to improve throughput ended up delaying emission when the KV cache warmup was slightly slower than expected.

What we’ve done so far:
- Rolled back the batching change on affected shards and rebalanced streaming workers across additional instances.
- Patched the KV cache warmup path to avoid blocking emission while population completes.
- Added a temporary routing rule to send critical customers to us-east-1 for the next 48 hours.

Customer next steps we recommend (short-term):
1) Keep the polling fallback for high-volume checkout flows for 24 hours to avoid UI flutters.
2) If you switch back to streaming, use `response_chunk_bytes:512` and `max_tokens:512` for the next 24–48 hours.

Planned follow-up:
- We’ll publish a full incident report (postmortem) by 2027-11-07 with timeline, full root cause analysis, and permanent mitigations.
- A remediation call is scheduled for 2027-11-05 10:00 AM PST — invite sent to your calendar.
- We will provide a one-time service credit covering the 23-minute impact window; the CS team will follow up with the formal credit note and MRR impact.

Attachments: runbook link and telemetry (see SR and Drive link). If you want, we can schedule an engineering deep-dive to walk through traces and telemetry.

Again — very sorry for the disruption. We’re treating this as a priority and will share the postmortem when ready.

Best,
